explain.what: Whether the share price is above or below its average price over the last ~10 months.
explain.why: Big funds buy and sell around this line, so being above it usually means buyers are in control. It is slow: it confirms a turn after it has happened.
explain.score: The price is above its long-run average: the long-term trend is up.

explain.what: Whether the shorter trend (last ~10 weeks) is running above or below the longer trend (last ~10 months).
explain.why: It shows whether the trend itself is turning, not just where the price is today.
explain.score: The shorter trend is above the longer one: momentum is building upward.

indicators.name: Relative strength vs peers, 3 months
indicators.measured: equal-weighted average of 6 peers over 63 trading days

explain.what: Whether the stock has done better or worse than its direct competitors over the last 3 months.
explain.why: It separates something specific to this company from a whole-industry move.
explain.score: Moving roughly in line with its competitors.

indicators.name: Buying vs selling volume
indicators.measured: volume on up days ÷ down days, last 20 trading days

explain.what: Whether more shares change hands on days the price rises than on days it falls (last 20 trading days).
explain.why: Large investors leave footprints in trading volume; heavy buying days suggest they are accumulating.
explain.score: Much more trading on up days: buyers are more active than sellers.

explain.what: How many shares are borrowed and sold by investors betting the price will fall, and whether that is growing.
explain.why: Short sellers often do deep research, so a rising number of bets against a stock is a warning worth noticing.
explain.score: Bets against the stock are growing, or are unusually large.

indicators.name: Institutional ownership change
indicators.measured: shares added minus shares cut by institutions last quarter, as % of shares outstanding
indicators.note: Proxy: counts changes in existing positions, not new or closed ones.

explain.what: Whether professional investment firms, in total, added or cut shares last quarter.
explain.why: Shows whether the big money is moving in or out. It arrives late (filings come up to 45 days after the quarter).
explain.score: Funds added a meaningful number of shares last quarter.

indicators.name: Dollar backdrop (shared macro)
indicators.measured: the dollar index 20 trading days earlier

explain.what: Whether the US dollar has strengthened or weakened over the last month.
explain.why: A strong dollar pulls money out of riskier assets worldwide and shrinks the dollar value of overseas sales.
explain.score: The dollar has strengthened: a headwind for stocks.

indicators.name: Fed rate expectations (shared macro)
indicators.measured: net odds (cut minus rise) for the next Fed meeting, 28 days earlier
indicators.note: Now: 1% cut, 16% rise; a month ago: 4% cut, 31% rise.

explain.what: Whether markets now expect the Fed to cut or raise interest rates at its next meeting, compared with a month ago.
explain.why: Interest rates set the price of every other asset; expectations move long before the Fed acts.

indicators.name: Revenue growth trend
indicators.measured: average growth of the prior 4 quarters, each vs a year earlier

explain.what: Whether sales growth is speeding up or slowing down compared with the past year.
explain.why: The plainest evidence of whether customers want more of what the company sells.

indicators.name: Gross margin trend
indicators.text: n/a (gross profit not filed for 8 quarters)
indicators.measured: gross margin of the 4 quarters a year earlier

explain.what: Whether the share of each sales dollar kept as gross profit is rising or falling.
explain.why: A company that can hold or raise its margins has pricing power, a sign of strong demand.
explain.score: No live data today, so it is left out of the score.

indicators.name: Earnings forecast revisions
indicators.measured: consensus EPS for the year to 2027-12-31, 90 days earlier

explain.what: Whether analysts have raised or cut their profit forecasts over the last 3 months.
explain.why: Changes in expected profit are one of the most reliable drivers of share prices over the following months.
explain.score: Analysts are raising their profit forecasts.

indicators.name: Forward P/E vs peers
indicators.measured: median of the peer set (next 12 months, same rule)
indicators.note: Next 12 months: blends consensus EPS for the years to 2026-12-31 and 2027-12-31 ($14.46). Yahoo's next-fiscal-year figure: 23.0x.

explain.what: How much investors pay for each dollar of the company's expected profit, compared with its competitors.
explain.why: Paying much more than for rivals means good news is already in the price, so there is less room for disappointment.
explain.score: Priced roughly in line with its competitors.

explain.what: The same comparison as above, but allowing for how fast profits are expected to grow.
explain.why: A higher price can be fair if profits grow faster; this checks whether they do.
explain.score: Its expected growth broadly explains the price.

indicators.name: EV/EBITDA vs peers
indicators.note: EV = market value + debt − cash ($4,127bn) ÷ last-12-month EBITDA ($173.2bn).

explain.what: The company's total value (including debt) compared with its operating profit, against competitors.
explain.why: Unlike the P/E, this counts debt, so an indebted company cannot look artificially cheap.
explain.score: More expensive than its competitors once debt is counted.

bullets: Demand is strong. Demand scores +62, unchanged from yesterday: Search & other revenue +16.8% and Google Cloud +81.8% (Apr-Jun 2026 vs a year earlier), both bullish; analysts' 2027 profit forecast $15.17 a share vs $14.53 90 days ago (+4.4%, bullish). Google's search share −0.4 points vs a year earlier (neutral). Revenue growth trend: 12.0% vs a 14.0% average for the prior four quarters (−1.9 points, neutral), also unchanged. Margin trend (DM6) is still blank: see Known defects.

Valuation is above peers, not extreme. Valuation scores −21, unchanged: forward P/E 24.0x vs a 20.1x peer median (+19%, neutral); growth-adjusted P/E 1.2 vs 1.1 (+14%, neutral); EV/EBITDA 23.8x vs 17.4x (+37%, bearish).

Money flows are mixed. Liquidity scores +20: buying volume 1.98x selling volume over 20 days and institutions added +1.14 points of shares (both bullish, though part of the institutional increase is new shares from the June equity raise); the dollar rose 2.99 points in 20 trading days (bearish). Short interest +20.7% in a month scores bearish, which is an engine defect for GOOG (see Known defects).

Price trend is positive but still behind peers. Price trend scores +72, up from +44: price $347.37 (+0.81% on the day vs −0.22% for the S&P 500), 2.8% above its 200-day average and the 50-day average 1.5% above the 200-day (both bullish); the 3-month return is 3.1 points behind the peers (neutral), up from 6.2 points behind yesterday (bearish); the bearish line is more than 5 points behind.

Not confirmed, and no longer on the line. Day 3 of history (3 of 10 trading days recorded): the call needs 7 of the last 10 trading days in one zone. Coverage 97% of the weight left after removals. At +37 it is 7 points above the +30 Buy line, but one indicator turning (forecast revisions or relative valuation) could still move it into the Hold zone; the revenue growth trend is 0.1 point from turning bearish (−1.9 vs the −2 line). defects: Staging tab, first built 6 Oct 2026: the call needs 7 of the last 10 trading days in one zone before it is confirmed.

DM6 (gross margin trend) is blank: Alphabet files no gross-profit line (not filed for 8 quarters). DM1 (revenue growth trend) was also blank until 6 Oct because Alphabet switched the SEC tag it files revenue under in 2025; it now computes (12.0% vs a 14.0% average, neutral). Fix logged for the Framework chat; until then 3 of Demand's 29 points are missing.

Reported EPS includes large paper gains on equity stakes ($2.35 a share in Q1 2026, $6.26 in Q2). VL3 (trailing P/E vs own history) is removed for this reason; forward P/E uses analysts' forecasts, which exclude the gains.
Cash conversion (operating cash ÷ net profit) will look weak once full-year 2026 is filed, because net profit includes the paper gains. It needs two weak years to flag.
DM5 (StatCounter search share) counts search engines only, not questions asked to ChatGPT or other chatbots. A steady share does not prove Search is safe; a falling share would be a strong warning.

EV/EBITDA does not subtract Alphabet's private and listed stakes (SpaceX about $94bn reported, Anthropic and others), which are in the share price but earn nothing in EBITDA. Allowing for $150-200bn of stakes would still leave GOOG about 30-32% above the peer median, past the 25% bearish line.
Caution from the 5-year replay: GOOG's price-trend signals had no useful order (Buy days were followed by below-average returns vs the S&P 500). Treat a call driven by price trend as weak evidence.
Holders and short interest are for GOOG (Class C) shares only.

LQ2 (short interest) scores bearish (+20.7% in a month) although only about 0.9% of GOOG shares are sold short (51.8m of 5,527m), below the 2% minimum. Yahoo gives no 'share of float' figure for GOOG, so the engine skips the 2% rule. Engine fix requested from the Framework chat; with it, Liquidity would read +40 and the composite about +40.

LQ3 divides the GOOG-only institutional change (+139.8m shares, Nasdaq) by all Alphabet shares (about 12.2bn, market value ÷ price), so it reads +1.14 points; on GOOG shares alone it is +2.5 points. Both are bullish, but part of the increase is new shares from the 2 Jun equity raise, not buying; without the 25.5m new public GOOG shares it would read +0.94 points on the current base (neutral). Holder percentages on the page are understated about 2.2x for the same reason.
Revenue mix: the reported parts miss total revenue by up to 0.9% in 2022 because of currency hedging gains, which Alphabet reports outside its revenue lines; shown as Other.

DM2 uses analysts' 2027 forecast (+4.4% in 90 days). Kenneth decided on 6 Oct that DM2 should use the next 12 months, as the plan says; the Framework chat will change the engine. On that blend (2026 cut 5.2%, 2027 raised 3.7%) DM2 is about +1.8% (neutral), Demand +40 and the composite about +30 (on the Buy line). The 2026 forecast covers only 6 analysts.
The score sits 7 points above the Buy line (+37 vs +30): DM2 turning neutral, VL1 moving about 6 points further above peers (bearish at +25%), or PT1 slipping would each move it into the Hold zone.

segments.name: Search & other
segments.sells: Ads shown next to Google Search results (including AI Overviews and AI Mode), Maps, Gmail and Play Store search.
segments.buyers: Advertisers of every size, from retailers and travel firms to banks and insurers, paying per click.
pos: The profit engine: 54.6% of revenue over the last 4 quarters, growing 16.8% vs the 4 quarters before.
Growth sped up from +11.7% (Q2 2025) to +16.8% (Q2 2026) despite AI chatbots: AI Mode passed 1 billion monthly users.
Shares the Google Services segment margin of 41.9% (last 4 quarters), vs Alphabet's reported operating margin of 33.1% after costs it does not allocate to segments.
neg: Most exposed to AI chatbots answering questions without ads (DM5 cannot see chatbot usage).
Antitrust remedies on default-search payments still under appeal (chain C4).
Not recurring: ad budgets can be cut quickly in a downturn.

segments.name: YouTube ads
segments.sells: Ads on YouTube videos, Shorts and YouTube on TV screens.
segments.buyers: Brand and performance advertisers; competes with TV, Netflix and Meta for ad budgets.
pos: $42.6bn over the last 4 quarters, +11.7% vs the 4 before; Q2 2026 +12.9%.
YouTube is the most-watched streaming service on US TV screens, pulling TV ad money.
neg: Growing slower than the company (+20.1%): share of revenue down from 10.3% to 9.6% in a year.
Cyclical: brand advertising is the first budget cut in a downturn.

segments.name: Google Network
segments.sells: Ads Google places on other companies' websites and apps (AdSense, AdMob, Ad Manager).
segments.buyers: Advertisers, with most of the money passed on to the website and app owners.
pos: Small and shrinking slowly: 6.6% of revenue, so its decline barely moves the total.
neg: Shrinking: −2.2% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before; its share fell from 10.9% to 6.6% in 3 years.
Ad-tech remedies (16 Sep 2026) force Google to open AdX to rival ad servers under a 6-year monitor (chain C4).
Its own margin is not disclosed (it shares the Google Services margin on this page), but most of its revenue is paid out to publishers, so its true margin is likely far lower.

segments.name: Subscriptions, platforms & devices
segments.sells: YouTube Premium and Music, YouTube TV, Google One storage and AI plans, Play Store fees, Pixel phones and devices.
segments.buyers: Consumers paying monthly, app developers paying store fees, phone buyers.
pos: Mostly monthly subscriptions: steady and growing 17.9% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before.
Google One AI plans add a way to charge for Gemini directly.
neg: Includes low-margin hardware (Pixel) and Play Store fees under legal pressure (Epic case).
Reported inside Google Services, so its own margin is not disclosed (it shares the Services margin on this page).

segments.name: Google Cloud
segments.sells: Cloud computing, AI chips (TPUs) and models (Gemini) rented to businesses, plus Workspace (Gmail, Docs for companies).
segments.buyers: Large companies, governments and AI labs, often on multi-year contracts.
pos: Fastest-growing part: +57.8% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before, +81.8% in Q2 2026.
Margin up from about 0% (4 quarters to Jun 2023) to 31.3% (last 4 quarters).
$514bn of signed orders not yet billed, more than 6 times the last 4 quarters' Cloud revenue ($77.6bn).
neg: Where the $195-205bn of 2026 capex must earn its return: if growth slows, depreciation will crush the margin (chain C1).
A few AI labs are large customers; Alphabet does not disclose how much of the backlog they hold.
Still below the Google Services margin (31.3% vs 41.9%).

segments.name: Other Bets
segments.sells: Waymo robotaxis, Verily (health), and other early-stage businesses.
segments.buyers: Waymo riders; health and other partners.
pos: Waymo is the leading US robotaxi service: an option on a large market.
neg: Losing money fast: −$8.9bn operating loss over the last 4 quarters vs −$4.8bn for the 4 before.

The shift in mix alone took 0.6 pts off segment operating margin vs a year earlier (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters a year earlier, each part's margin held at that earlier level).
The shift in mix alone took 2.3 pts off segment operating margin vs 3 years earlier (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters 3 years earlier, each part's margin held at that earlier level).
Fastest-growing part (Google Cloud, +58% vs a year earlier) earns below the company segment operating margin.
Concentration: Search & other is 55% of sales (last 4 quarters).

shift.title: What the shift means for Alphabet
pos: Cloud rose from 10.2% to 17.4% of revenue in 3 years (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters to Jun 2023), and its margin from about 0% to 31.3%.
Alphabet's reported operating margin rose from 25.7% to 33.1% over the same 3 years (after costs not allocated to segments).
Less dependent on the declining Network business (10.9% → 6.6% of revenue).
neg: Search is still 54.6% of revenue and most of the profit: the AI-chatbot risk is concentrated in one part.
Cloud's margin (31.3%) is below Services' (41.9%), so as Cloud grows the mix alone slightly pulls the company margin down.
Other Bets losses nearly doubled in a year (−$8.9bn vs −$4.8bn, last 4 quarters).

mix.note: Alphabet reports operating profit for three segments only: Google Services (Search, YouTube ads, Network, Subscriptions), Google Cloud and Other Bets. So the four Services parts all show the Google Services margin. Hedging gains and losses are not a part (shown as Other when material). The 'whole company' margin in the mix table is the segment total before Alphabet's unallocated costs (e.g. part of AI research); Alphabet's reported operating margin is lower.
checks: Reported parts miss the total by up to 0.9% of revenue: shown as Other.
